outcome: acute postpartum admission to theatre/high dependency unit/intensive care unit (<12hr post birth)
acute neonatal admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU; <12hr post birth)
cohort: 4,207 low-risk women who gave birth in either a tertiary maternity hospital or one of three primary maternity units in South Auckland, New Zealand.
finding: Low-risk women giving birth in primary maternity units had fewer emergency caesarean sections, postpartum haemorrhages, acute postpartum admissions, and their babies were less likely to have a low Apgar score or require admission to NICU compared to those giving birth in a tertiary maternity hospital.
